By adding header support to StreamPartitioner, we ensure that headers are consistently available throughout the Kafka Streams processing pipeline—from the source, through transformations and state stores (as per KIP-1271), to final partitioning and serialization.

Proposed Changes

  1. Interface Enhancement: Add the headers-aware partitions method to StreamPartitioner. This is a default method to ensure binary compatibility.
  2. Public API for Interactive Queries: Add new overloads to KafkaStreams#queryMetadataForKey that accept `Headers`. This allows users to perform metadata lookups for header-dependent partitioning strategies

  3. Headers Mutability and Nullability: While headers are mutable by nature, StreamPartitioner is not expected to mutate them. The documentation will explicitly mention that mutating headers can lead to unexpected results. Additionally, when using StreamPartitioner or Interactive Queries (IQ), headers can be empty, but they cannot be null. This behavior will also be explicitly documented

  4. No changes are planed for KafkaStreamsNamedTopologyWrapper. This class and entire feature are deprecated, so no changes are planed there
  5. Internal Callers and Propagation:
    1. RecordCollectorImpl#send to pass record headers when calling the partitioner.
    2. StreamsMetadataState to support the new header-aware lookups.
  6. Built-in Implementations:

    1. WindowedStreamPartitioner: Override the new method to propagate headers to the underlying WindowedSerializer#serializeBaseKey. 

    2. DefaultStreamPartitioner: Override the new method to propagate headers to the keySerializer#serialize . 

Compatibility, Deprecation, and Migration Plan

Backward Compatibility (API Level)

This change is fully backward-compatible from an API and compilation perspective. The new header-aware partitions method is added as a default method on the StreamPartitioner  interface, and it safely delegates to the deprecated header-less method. Therefore, if users already have their own custom StreamPartitioner implementations, they will continue to compile and function exactly as before without any changes.

Behavioral Changes (Built-in Partitioners)

While the interface remains backward-compatible, the built-in Kafka Streams partitioners ( DefaultStreamPartitioner  and WindowedStreamPartitioner ) have been explicitly updated to leverage the new API. They do not delegate to the deprecated method. Instead, they implement the new header-aware method and propagate the real record Headers  directly to the underlying key serializer.

Migration Action for Header-Sensitive Serializers

Because DefaultStreamPartitioner  and WindowedStreamPartitioner  now pass actual headers to the underlying key serializer (instead of empty/no headers), there is a behavioral shift for users who use header-sensitive serializers (serializers whose output changes depending on the headers).

  • Impact: For these users, the serialized byte array will change, meaning the partition assignment for records will silently change upon upgrading. This will break co-partitioning with any data written prior to the upgrade.
  • Action: To preserve the old partitioning behavior and maintain co-partitioning, affected users can no longer rely on the built-in partitioners. They will need to create their own custom StreamPartitioner  that explicitly strips the headers (e.g., by passing empty headers) before delegating to their serializer.

Deprecation and Functional Interface Migration

  • The header-less partitions methods are deprecated for removal in Kafka 5.0. To prevent internal bugs, built-in partitioners ( DefaultStreamPartitioner , WindowedStreamPartitioner , etc.) now explicitly throw an UnsupportedOperationException  if their deprecated header-less partitions method is called.
  • StreamPartitioner  is currently a functional interface targeting the deprecated method. Users using lambda syntax will see deprecation warnings. To avoid these warnings, users should migrate from lambdas to anonymous or concrete classes that override the new header-aware method. Once the deprecated method is removed in 5.0, the interface will target the new method, and users can safely return to using lambda syntax.

Test Plan

  • Unit Tests and Integration tests:
    • Verify Partitioners correctly propagate headers.
    • Verify propagated headers are used to determine target partition

Rejected Alternatives

  • Updated the existing method without default: Rejected as it would break all existing user implementations.
